result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection with marked high-visibility crosswalks and traffic signals. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and signals are present, the wide crossing distance and lack of physical protection like refuge islands or curb extensions increase pedestrian exposure.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median or refuge island, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Wide Curb Radii
hazards.description: The corner design allows for high-speed vehicle turns, increasing the risk of collisions with pedestrians in the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right and left corners of the intersection

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a protected island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Add high-visibility pedestrian crossing signs or RRFBs to alert drivers to the presence of the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking or obstructions near the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.
